entries.title: Physiology and Pathology of Aging

testable_competencies.aging_physiology_overview: Recognize normal age-related organ-system physiologic change as background for the geriatric syndrome units that follow.

entries.zero_question_reason: Normal physiology/aging background; not independently testable but frames later syndrome-specific units.

entries.title: Framework for the Approach to the Older Adult (Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 31-1's key objective explicitly requires the candidate to 'conduct an assessment of function and cognition' and demonstrate 'awareness of the importance of a multidisciplinary approach' for a frail older adult - this unit is the chapter's general multidimensional-assessment framework that operationalizes that requirement, though the objective itself is scoped to frailty specifically rather than to the assessment framework as its own competency.

testable_competencies.multidimensional_assessment: Apply a structured, multidimensional approach (function, cognition, mobility, mood, social supports, medications) to the assessment of an older adult, distinct from a single-system history and physical.
testable_competencies.capacity_distinction: Distinguish clinical assessment of cognition/function from legal decision-making capacity, consent, and substitute decision-making, which remain the domain of ELOM pending final cross-chapter ownership resolution.

entries.title: Constipation in Older Adults

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 16-1 requires diagnosing cause, severity, and complications of adult constipation and initiating management; this GM unit shares the same objective but its distinct content is the age-specific contributing-factor profile (polypharmacy, immobility, low fluid/fibre intake, cognitive impairment affecting recognition), not a separate MCC-tested competency.

testable_competencies.geriatric_risk_factors: Identify age-specific contributing factors (medications, immobility, dehydration, cognitive impairment) that materially change the assessment of constipation in an older adult versus a general adult.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Chapter G (completed) already covers adult constipation generally via SU-G-25 under the same MCC objective (16-1); PRIMARY_OWNER=G for general etiology/management, CROSS_LINK=GM for the geriatric-specific contributing-factor context (polypharmacy, immobility, cognition) - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit, final ownership not resolved here.

entries.title: Delirium

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 58-2's key objective is an exact match: 'Given a patient with delirium, a candidate will recognize the syndrome, diagnose the cause(s), and will initiate an appropriate management plan. Particular attention should be paid to the urgent nature of the condition.' Older adults are the population at highest baseline risk, making this a core geriatric competency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Distinguishing delirium from underlying dementia is the central diagnostic challenge in older adults and is explicitly the pairing MCC groups under objective 58 (Delirium and dementia); cited here as the required comparator, not as this unit's primary content.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize delirium (acute onset, fluctuating course, inattention, altered level of consciousness) and distinguish it from dementia and depression in an older adult.
testable_competencies.workup_management: Identify precipitating/predisposing causes and initiate an urgent, cause-directed management plan, including non-pharmacologic measures first-line.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Delirium overlaps Psychiatry and Neurology (not yet mapped), which may cover its psychiatric/neurologic mechanism and differential in more depth; GM's content is the geriatric-population recognition, urgency, and multifactorial-cause angle. PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 114-2 is an exact title/content match: 'Given an older adult in a state of distress or presenting with unexplained findings, the candidate will inquire about potential abuse... determine the level of immediate risk, identify potential contributing factors, and outline an appropriate management plan.'

testable_competencies.recognition_and_response: Recognize clinical findings suggestive of elder abuse (physical, psychological, financial, neglect), assess immediate risk, and outline an appropriate safety and reporting plan.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 32 is an exact match: 'Given a patient who is at risk of falls, the candidate will identify contributing factors and initiate an appropriate management and prevention plan.'

testable_competencies.risk_assessment: Identify intrinsic (sensory, cognitive, musculoskeletal, medication) and extrinsic (environmental) fall risk factors in an older adult.
testable_competencies.prevention_plan: Initiate an appropriate falls-prevention and management plan, including medication review and referral where indicated.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 31-1 is an exact match: 'Given a frail older adult, the candidate will diagnose the cause, severity, and complications, will conduct an assessment of function and cognition, and will initiate an appropriate management plan that demonstrates an awareness of the importance of a multidisciplinary approach.'

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize frailty as a distinct clinical syndrome (e.g., unintentional weight loss, exhaustion, weakness, slow gait, low activity) rather than normal aging.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate a multidisciplinary management plan addressing the identified contributing domains.

entries.title: Immobility

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective addresses immobility as its own presentation. Objective 31-1's required 'assessment of function' is the nearest adjacent evidence, since immobility is a core component/consequence of frailty and a driver of falls (objective 32), but neither objective names immobility explicitly.

testable_competencies.immobility_cycle: Recognize immobility as both a contributor to and a consequence of falls, frailty, and functional decline in hospitalized or deconditioned older adults.

entries.zero_question_reason: Immobility is a contributing factor/complication addressed within the Falls and Frailty objectives rather than an independently MCC-tested competency; retained as a distinct unit only because Toronto Notes gives it independent topic status.

entries.title: Incontinence in Older Adults (Urinary and Fecal)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 47-2 requires diagnosing cause, severity, and complications of adult urinary incontinence and addressing stress and urge subtypes; this GM unit adds the geriatric-specific transient-cause framework (e.g., delirium, infection, restricted mobility, stool impaction, pharmaceuticals) on top of the same objective.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 47-1 explicitly recognizes incontinence as multifactorial, including due to disease affecting cognition or mobility - directly relevant to the geriatric-specific mechanism emphasized in this unit.

testable_competencies.transient_causes: Apply a geriatric-specific transient-cause framework (e.g., delirium, restricted mobility, stool impaction, infection, pharmaceuticals, psychological) before assuming an established/chronic urologic or gynecologic cause.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Urology and Gynecology (both not yet mapped) are expected to cover the full structural/urodynamic workup of incontinence in more depth; GM's content is the geriatric transient-cause and functional-context angle. PRIMARY_OWNER not finalized here - recorded for the global chapter-overlap audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 118-2's causal-conditions list names 'decreased nutritional intake' and chronic-illness-related caloric deficit; geriatric malnutrition most often presents as unintentional weight loss, though the objective is not scoped to older adults specifically or named 'malnutrition'.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize malnutrition risk in an older adult (unintentional weight loss, reduced intake, social/functional barriers to eating) and initiate an appropriate nutritional assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 40's causal-conditions list explicitly names presbycusis under sensorineural hearing loss ('Acquired (e.g., presbycusis, noise-induced hearing loss, ototoxicity)'); this unit is the age-related-etiology component of the broader hearing-loss objective.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize presbycusis as the most common cause of sensorineural hearing loss in older adults and its downstream functional/social impact (communication, isolation, safety).

entries.title: Presbyopia (Age-Related Vision Changes)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize presbyopia as a normal, near-universal age-related refractive change (lens stiffening reducing accommodation), distinct from pathological chronic visual loss.

entries.zero_question_reason: Objective 115-2 (Chronic visual disturbance/loss)'s causal-conditions list names only pathological causes (glaucoma, cataracts, macular degeneration, chronic-illness retinopathy) and does not name presbyopia, a normal age-related refractive change rather than a disease process; no adequate MCC evidence was found and none was fabricated.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38 requires diagnosing the cause, severity, and complications of a skin/integument condition; pressure injuries are a skin/integument condition but are not named explicitly in the retrieved excerpt, so this is treated as the general category rather than a name-specific match.

testable_competencies.staging_and_prevention: Recognize pressure injury risk factors and staging, and initiate an appropriate prevention/management plan in an immobile or hospitalized older adult.

entries.title: Driving Competency in Older Adults

testable_competencies.impairing_conditions: Recognize medical conditions (cognitive impairment, visual/hearing loss, certain medications, seizure disorders) that may impair fitness to drive in an older adult.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective (Medical Expert or role-level) was found addressing driving-fitness assessment or mandatory reporting; physician reporting obligations for medically unfit drivers are set provincially/territorially in Canada, not Canada-wide, so no province-neutral question could be written without inventing a rule. Flagged for future jurisdiction-specific verification rather than tested at this scope stage.

entries.title: Hazards of Hospitalization (Healthcare Institutions)

testable_competencies.iatrogenic_risk_awareness: Recognize institutional/iatrogenic risks specific to hospitalized older adults (deconditioning, delirium precipitation, nosocomial infection, functional decline) as a rationale for minimizing avoidable hospitalization and restraint/catheter/bedrest use.

entries.zero_question_reason: No dedicated MCC objective addresses hospitalization hazards as its own tested presentation; content is background context that motivates management choices already tested within the syndrome-specific units (delirium, immobility, pressure injuries, falls).

entries.title: Pharmacokinetic and Pharmacodynamic Changes in Aging

testable_competencies.mechanistic_background: Recognize age-related changes in pharmacokinetics (volume of distribution, hepatic/renal clearance) and pharmacodynamics (receptor sensitivity) as the mechanistic basis for altered drug dosing in older adults.

entries.zero_question_reason: Mechanistic pharmacology background; not independently testable but underlies the applied polypharmacy/prescribing unit (SU-GM-17), which carries the tested MCC evidence.

entries.title: Polypharmacy and Inappropriate Prescribing in Older Adults

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 125's enabling objectives explicitly require the candidate to 'address polypharmacy and the options for deprescribing' and to 'address the effect of comorbidities, current medications, liver and renal function, genetics, age... on the risks and benefits of prescribing the medication' - a direct match to this unit's polypharmacy/deprescribing and inappropriate-prescribing content.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Leader/Manager - Abide by the regulatory requirements governing medical office practice (maintenance of patient records, guidelines concerning prescriptions, especially narcotics)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (role-level record; no per-objective ID exists for this role)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Group's enabling text names prescribing-regulation compliance generically; the deprescribing/inappropriate-prescribing frameworks in this unit are the geriatric-specific operationalization of that broader prescribing-safety obligation, though the objective does not name geriatric prescribing tools (e.g., Beers/STOPP-START-type criteria) specifically.

testable_competencies.polypharmacy_recognition: Recognize polypharmacy and potentially inappropriate medications as a contributing cause of falls, delirium, and other geriatric syndromes covered elsewhere in this chapter.
testable_competencies.deprescribing: Apply a structured medication-review/deprescribing approach in an older adult with polypharmacy.

entries.title: Common Geriatric Medications (Reference)
do_not_test: Reference medication-summary table - drug names/doses/classes are reference material duplicating each syndrome unit's own management content, not an independent competency.
entries.zero_question_reason: Reference material duplicating syndrome-unit management content; per project scope rules, exact current treatment recommendations are not encoded at this scope stage.

entries.title: Landmark Geriatric Medicine Trials (Reference)
entries.zero_question_reason: Bibliographic/trial-summary reference content, not an independently testable clinical competency.
